fact: WebSocket bridge must handle both NDJSON (Claude Code) and JSON-RPC (Codex) protocols
recommendation: Always test protocol changes against both backends

fact: Session state persists to $TMPDIR/vibe-sessions/ as JSON and survives server restarts
recommendation: Test session recovery after server restart when changing session-related code

fact: Every frontend component must have .test.tsx with render + axe a11y scan
recommendation: Create test file alongside component, include toHaveNoViolations()

fact: Validate every JSONL line after a schema migration with json.loads + required-field set diff
recommendation: After bulk-rewriting .agents/knowledge/*.jsonl, pipe each file through `python3 -c` that does json.loads on every non-empty line and asserts the required-fields set is a subset of the keys. Catches truncated lines, missed fields, and trailing-comma fixes that look fine to the eye.

provenance.reference: commit 16f47e5 — schema migration validated via python3 one-liner before push

fact: Think before coding: state assumptions explicitly, surface tradeoffs, ask when unclear instead of picking silently
recommendation: Before any non-trivial change, name your assumptions, present alternatives if multiple interpretations exist, and stop to ask if something is genuinely ambiguous. Don't hide confusion behind plausible-looking code.

fact: Simplicity first: write the minimum code that solves the problem; no speculative abstractions, flexibility, or error handling for impossible cases
recommendation: If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite. Avoid abstractions for single-use code. Ask 'would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?' — if yes, simplify before submitting.

fact: Surgical changes: every changed line should trace directly to the user's request; don't 'improve' adjacent code, comments, or formatting
recommendation: When editing existing code, match its style even if you'd write it differently. Only remove imports/vars that YOUR change orphaned. Mention unrelated dead code, don't delete it unprompted.

fact: Goal-driven execution: transform tasks into verifiable success criteria so the loop can close itself
recommendation: Convert imperative requests into declarative goals: 'add validation' → 'write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass'. For multi-step work, write the brief plan with a verify step per item before starting.

fact: Every long-running async invocation needs a verifiable termination condition defined BEFORE launch
recommendation: Before any run_in_background=true call, write down 'how will I know this is done?'. No answer -> must use foreground with explicit timeout. Synthesises got-003/anti-003 with Karpathy goal-driven execution (pat-karpathy-004): open loops become zombies.

fact: Claude Code hook scripts must be registered in settings.json hooks.<Event>[].hooks[].command to be active — file existence alone does not activate them
recommendation: After authoring a hook script, grep settings.json for the script basename to verify wiring. Document hook activation in the skill's SKILL.md and provide explicit settings.json snippet.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-10 aura-companion: self-improvement/scripts/{activator,error-detector}.sh existed 16 days unwired — autonomy never worked

fact: Stop-hook loop safety: write the per-session marker file BEFORE emitting the {decision:block} JSON, not after
recommendation: Pattern: touch /tmp/<hook>-${SESSION_ID} before echo of block JSON. Race-safe: prevents infinite block loop even if Claude races to next Stop quickly. Always early-exit on empty SESSION_ID.

fact: Centralize cross-project bulk-write allow rules in ~/.claude/settings.json (user tier) via glob paths; reserve .claude/settings.local.json for project-specific exceptions — never blanket-allow Write or Edit
recommendation: For dirs that follow a stable cross-project convention (auto-memory at /root/.claude/projects/*/memory/**, knowledge bases at /root/*/.agents/knowledge/**, learning logs at /root/*/.learnings/**) put Write(<glob>/**) + Edit(<glob>/**) in ~/.claude/settings.json — one entry, all projects, all future repos auto-covered. Allow Read/Glob/Grep without scope at the same tier (low risk). Use .claude/settings.local.json only for one-off project paths that don't fit a cross-project pattern. NEVER blanket-allow Write or Edit — one bad edit to src/** costs more than one extra prompt. Path-rule syntax supports * (single segment) and ** (recursive).

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 user request: 'неужели нельзя чтобы подобное было централизовано от всей системы?' — moved per-project rules to ~/.claude/settings.json

fact: Same-project dual-session pipeline: orchestrator + observer with filesystem-mediated handoff via phases/<N>/<NN>-<phase>.md
recommendation: For auto-pipelines spanning spec→plan→implement→review→ship, run TWO sessions in same project: (1) orchestrator runs /spec-writer → /council-* skills in sequence, writes artifacts to phases/<N>/ directory; (2) observer ScheduleWakeup-polls phases/, reads new artifacts, writes <NN>-observer-review.md, drops phases/<N>/STOP.md as halt signal. Both sessions need bypassPermissions (Agent mode) for true zero-click. Termination = orchestrator stops at human ship gate before push. Same-project observer outperforms 'external eye in different project' for find-real-bugs work IF observer follows EC-6 discipline (grep claims, push back on subjective findings, enforce role: do NOT push even if user mistypes 'go').

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 auraengine Phase 1.5 PR #89 — Fleet Summit-2 + Verdant Flint

fact: Pipeline experiments need explicit propagation timing rule in orchestrator prompt: 'after ship' vs 'after pipeline complete' — these differ
recommendation: When prompting an auto-pipeline orchestrator with cross-project memory propagation rules, be explicit about WHEN propagation fires. 'After pipeline complete' (= reached human ship gate) and 'after ship confirmed' (= PR merged) are different — orchestrator will interpret reasonably but may pick the earlier moment. For ship-gated propagation, use phrase 'propagate ONLY after operator confirms PR merged + deployed' or use a sentinel file (phases/SHIPPED.md) the orchestrator must wait for.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 auraengine Phase 1.5 — orchestrator propagated 4 learnings before push (defensible interpretation of 'end of pipeline')

fact: For skill packs with hard-coded subagent panels in SKILL.md (e.g. Carmack Council), fork into a suffixed sibling directory rather than replacing in-place
recommendation: When adapting a skill like council-{plan,review,implement} to a different stack: create council-{plan,review,implement}-aura/ (or -<stackname>/) as new directories at the same tier (user-level /home/<user>/.claude/skills/). Copy all references/ files (cp, not symlinks — Claude Code skill loader is not guaranteed to follow symlinks). Update YAML description, Stack Context block, Phase 0 verification commands, and every Phase 3 subagent dispatch block. Trigger via /council-*-<stackname> slash command. Other projects keep using the original. Identification key: any SKILL.md whose description hard-codes a panel of named experts.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 Aura Companion fork of council-{plan,review,implement} into council-{plan,review,implement}-aura with 13-expert panel (6 kept, 4 retargeted, 3 new stack-specific)

fact: Reference docs in skill packs replicate by cp across sibling skill directories — do not symlink and do not single-source
recommendation: When a skill pack has multiple SKILL.md files (council-plan/, council-review/, council-implement/) sharing references/, write each reference once in the canonical dir, then `cp /home/<user>/.claude/skills/SOURCE/references/*.md /home/<user>/.claude/skills/SIBLING/references/`. Two reasons: (1) Claude Code skill loader semantics for symlinks are not documented — assume worst case (won't follow). (2) Single-source via SKILL.md ref like `../council-review-aura/references/security.md` couples the skills; if one is moved or renamed, the others break silently. Cost of duplication: ~3× disk for the same text, easily refreshed by re-running the cp on edits. For 13 references × 3 dirs the duplication is ~12k lines but each dir is self-contained.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 council-*-aura fork — 13 refs replicated to 3 sibling skill dirs via cp

fact: council-review-aura dispatch-skip-zero-domain pattern: skip experts with zero in-scope files rather than have them confirm 'no findings'
recommendation: On a server-only feature (e.g. Council Mode Tasks 1-9 which had no UI/no Dockerfile/no workflow changes), dispatch only 8 of the 13 experts: Hunt, Fowler, Bun/Hono/TS, FS-JSON Persistence, Realtime, Subprocess, Willison, Beck. Skip React/Web UI, a11y Auditor, Saarinen, Friedman, Docker/GHA. The SKILL.md explicitly says this — never spawn an expert whose domain has zero files in scope. Saves ~5 subagent runs (≈10-15min wall-clock) per scoped review. Conversely: 13/13 dispatch is for explicit full-repo review, not scoped diffs.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 /council-review-aura against Council Mode Tasks 1-9: 8/13 experts dispatched, 70 raw findings synthesized to 15

fact: Council Carmack filter ratio: ~70 raw expert findings synthesize to ~15 prioritised — aggressive dedup + cross-ref clustering is mandatory
recommendation: When the 8-13 council subagents return, expect 50-100 raw findings on a PR-scale review. The 15-cap is hard. Dedup strategy: (1) identify clusters where 3+ experts independently flag the same root cause (in the 2026-05-11 review: observer-profile-not-wired was flagged by Subprocess + Hunt + Willison + Beck) — keep ONE primary with cross-refs, even if losing per-expert framing. (2) Apply Carmack filter to demote 'real but low-probability' P1s (e.g. `writeSync` short-write at 256 KiB is theoretical, demote to P2). (3) Fold Beck's test-side findings into cross-refs on production gaps where the test gap = the same root cause. Final composition target: ~50% P1, ~33% P2, ~17% P3 on a feature-sized review.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 review: 70 raw → 15 final (8 P1 / 5 P2 / 2 P3). Beck's 11 findings folded entirely into cross-refs.
